business_model.claim: Hafnia generates revenue by providing seaborne transportation of refined oil, other petroleum products, and certain chemical products to international and national oil companies, major chemical companies, and trading and utility companies.
quotes: We are one of the world’s largest operators of chemical and product tankers and provide transportation of oil and oil products to leading international oil companies and national oil companies, major chemical companies, as well as trading and utility companies.
We generate revenue by charging our customers for the transportation of their refined oil products, other petroleum products, and chemical products using our Hafnia Vessels and TC Vessels.

business_model.claim: The company relies on its top five customers for a significant share of its revenue.
quotes: We derive a significant portion of our revenue from our top five customers, and the loss or default of any such customers could result in a significant loss of revenue and adversely affect our business.

business_model.basis: stated in F2, P1, P3, and P5
business_model.claim: Alongside vessel transport, Hafnia earns management fees on external vessels in its pools (recorded in other operating income of 31,101 in 2025, table in thousands; fee-based earnings of USD 16.6 million in the first half of 2026) and operates a 50% bunker procurement joint venture with Cargill that serviced approximately 2,400 vessels in 2025.
quotes: We account for the management fees we receive on External Vessels (Pool Vessels and JV Vessels employed in the Pools) as other operating income.
We and Cargill each have 50% of the outstanding equity in the Seascale Energy Joint Venture.
Since commencing operations in May 2025, the Seascale Energy Joint Venture serviced approximately 2,400 vessels during the year.
The fee-based businesses generated earnings of USD 16.6 million2 (H1 2025: USD 15.8 million).

business_model.claim: Revenue comes primarily from single-voyage spot charters, where Hafnia pays voyage and vessel operating expenses, and fixed-period time charters of six months or more, where the charterer pays voyage expenses.
quotes: Revenue primarily consists of revenue from voyage charters and time charters.
Under a spot market voyage charter, the vessel owner pays for the voyage expenses (less specified amounts covered by the contract), including bunker and port costs, and the vessel operating expenses.

Under a time charter, vessels are chartered to customers for a fixed period of time at rates that are generally fixed, but may contain a variable component based on inflation, interest rates or changes in current market rates.

business_model.claim: Most Hafnia and time-chartered-in vessels trade through nine commercial pools with profit sharing among participants; in 2025, gross revenue was $ 1,421,831 for Hafnia and TC vessels and 860,078 for external vessels in Disponent-Owner Pools, totaling $ 2,281,909 (table in thousands).
quotes: The majority of our Hafnia Vessels and TC Vessels are employed on voyage charters and time charters through our Pools, whereby earnings are subject to profit sharing with other pool participants.

We recognise gross revenue for all vessels employed in such Pools, in Revenue (Hafnia Vessels and TC Vessels) for our Hafnia Vessels and TC Vessels, and Revenue (External Vessels in Disponent-Owner Pools) for the External Vessels.
Revenue, voyage expenses and pool distributions in relation to External Vessels in Disponent-Owner Pools nets to zero, and therefore the calculation of TCE income is unaffected by these items:

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P2, and P3
business_model.claim: As at December 31, 2025, Hafnia operated a Combined Fleet of 187 vessels (99 Hafnia Vessels, 9 TC Vessels, 16 JV Vessels, and 61 third-party Pool Vessels, plus other commercially managed vessels), with 74% of the Hafnia Fleet in the short-term spot market and 85 Hafnia and TC vessels in pools or spot charters versus 23 on time charters.
quotes: As at December 31, 2025, we operated a Combined Fleet of 187 vessels (including the Hafnia Fleet (Hafnia Vessels, TC Vessels and JV Vessels), Pool Vessels and other commercially managed third-party vessels) of which 99 are Hafnia Vessels; 9 are TC Vessels and 16 are JV Vessels (including one newbuild in our Ecomar Joint Venture).

In addition to our Hafnia Fleet, as at December 31, 2025, we operated 61 Pool Vessels owned by third parties through our Pools and from time to time commercially manage additional vessels for third parties.
As at December 31, 2025, 74% of the vessels in our Hafnia Fleet were operated in the spot market on short-term contracts that normally do not extend beyond three months.

As at December 31, 2025, 85 of our Hafnia Vessels and TC Vessels were operating in the Pools or on spot charters outside the Pools and 23 were operating on time charter-out agreements outside of the Pools.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P3, and P5
business_model.claim: Hafnia manages and reports its business across four vessel-size segments—LR2, LR1, MR (including Chemical-MR), and Handy (including Chemical-Handy)—and plans to wind down its Handy and LR2 pools, exiting the Handy segment after vessel sales while placing most owned LR2 vessels on time charters.
quotes: Previously, we reported on “Chemical-MR” vessels and “Chemical-Handy” vessels as separate segments, however we have now grouped “Chemical-MR” and “Chemical-Handy” vessels under the MR segment and the Handy segment, respectively.

The Group’s revenue is generated from the following operating segments: LR2 Product Tankers, LR1 Product Tankers, MR Product Tankers (inclusive of IMO II vessels) and Handy Product Tankers (inclusive of IMO II vessels).
We intend to wind down our Handy and LR2 pool operations in the upcoming financial year.
We will exit the Handy segment upon the completion of the sale of our Handy vessels, while the majority of its owned LR2 vessels will be employed via time charters.

business_model.claim: Revenue is driven by hire or freight rates and operating days, with fleet utilisation (93.6% in 2025 versus 97.7% in 2024) reduced by technical off-hire from drydockings and repairs, including approximately 392 scheduled drydocking off-hire days in the second quarter of 2026.
quotes: Revenue is affected by hire/freight rates and the number of operating days a vessel operates.
Our utilisation rates are therefore primarily affected by planned and unplanned drydocking and other repairs, surveys, and maintenance.
Results for the quarter were impacted by approximately 392 off-hire vessel days related to scheduled drydockings, and we anticipate approximately 225 off-hire days in Q3.

business_model.basis: stated in P2, P3, and P5
business_model.claim: With high spot exposure, TCE revenue fluctuates with winter-stronger and summer-weaker seasonality, global tanker supply (a product tanker newbuild orderbook equal to approximately 18% of the world fleet at the end of 2025), and route disruptions such as Strait of Hormuz closures and Red Sea attacks that lengthened voyages and lifted average fleet TCE from $25,205 per day in 2025 to USD 44,093 per day in the second quarter of 2026.
quotes: The product tanker newbuild orderbook equalled approximately 18% of the existing world product tanker fleet in tonnage terms at the end of 2025.

Tanker markets are typically stronger in the winter months as a result of increased oil consumption and weather delays in the northern hemisphere but weaker in the summer months as a result of lower oil consumption in the northern hemisphere and refinery maintenance that is typically conducted in the summer months.
For the product tanker market, this has led to sustained fragmentation of global trade, with volumes East of Suez remaining constrained and alternative routings adding substantial voyage distance.
Our average fleet TCE for Q2 was USD 44,093 per day.

business_model.claim: Under spot voyage charters and Disponent-Owner Pools, Hafnia incurs voyage expenses—primarily bunker fuel, port costs, canal tolls, cargo handling, brokerage commissions, and pool adjustments—of (465,957) for Hafnia and TC vessels and (329,566) for external pool vessels in 2025, alongside pool distributions of $ (530,512) to external vessel owners (table in thousands).
quotes: Voyage expenses primarily include bunker and port expenses, as well as other voyage expenses such as canal tolls, cargo handling operations, brokerage commissions and the pool-allocated profit-sharing adjustment (pool allocation).

Importantly, our pool employment strategy will also allow us to directly benefit from the anticipated fuel savings of our newbuild vessels, as under spot market voyage charters we are responsible for all voyage expenses, including bunker fuel costs, which are generally the largest expense.
Pool distributions are distributed to the owners of External Vessels in the Disponent-Owner Pools.

business_model.claim: For owned and bareboat-leased Hafnia Vessels, the company bears vessel operating expenses of (282,123) in 2025—driven mainly by crewing, repairs and maintenance, and insurance—plus charter hire expenses of (33,415) for short-term chartered-in tonnage and depreciation of (201,702) including capitalised drydockings conducted every 30 to 60 months (table in thousands).
quotes: The three largest components of our vessel operating expenses are crewing, repairs and maintenance and insurance expenses.
We expect these expenses to increase as our fleet matures and to the extent that it expands.
Generally, each vessel is drydocked every 30 months to 60 months.
For TC Vessels, the owner is responsible for vessel operating expenses.

business_model.basis: stated in F1, F2, and P2
business_model.claim: Additional recurring cost drivers include technical management expenses of (27,082), other expenses of (84,876), and interest expense of (49,768) in 2025 (table in thousands), alongside borrowings of 910,402 non-current and 212,574 current at Dec. 31, 2025 (table in thousands).
quotes: Technical management expenses | (27,082) | (28,173) | (25,692)

We have a significant amount of financial debt and servicing our current or future indebtedness limits funds available for other purposes and if we cannot service our debt, we may lose the vessels in our Hafnia Fleet.

competitive_position.claim: Hafnia Limited is one of the world’s largest operators of chemical and product tankers, transporting oil, oil products, and chemicals for leading oil, chemical, trading, and utility companies.
quotes: We are one of the world’s largest operators of chemical and product tankers and provide transportation of oil and oil products to leading international oil companies and national oil companies, major chemical companies, as well as trading and utility companies.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 20-F Item 4 Business Overview.
competitive_position.claim: Hafnia operated a Combined Fleet of 187 vessels, comprising 99 Hafnia Vessels, 9 TC Vessels, 16 JV Vessels, and 61 third-party Pool Vessels plus other commercially managed third-party vessels.
quotes: As at December 31, 2025, we operated a Combined Fleet of 187 vessels (including the Hafnia Fleet (Hafnia Vessels, TC Vessels and JV Vessels), Pool Vessels and other commercially managed third-party vessels) of which 99 are Hafnia Vessels; 9 are TC Vessels and 16 are JV Vessels (including one newbuild in our Ecomar Joint Venture).

In addition to our Hafnia Fleet, as at December 31, 2025, we operated 61 Pool Vessels owned by third parties through our Pools and from time to time commercially manage additional vessels for third parties.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 20-F Item 4 and October 2026 Form 6-K.
competitive_position.claim: Hafnia operates a fully integrated shipping platform with in-house commercial management across its Combined Fleet apart from Andromeda Joint Venture vessels, and in-house technical management for 57 of its Hafnia Vessels and JV Vessels while third-party managers handle the remaining 57.
quotes: As owners and operators of around 180 vessels, we offer a fully integrated shipping platform, including technical management, commercial and chartering services, pool management, and a large-scale bunker procurement desk.

We provide in-house commercial management to all of the vessels in our Combined Fleet apart from the vessels in the Andromeda Joint Venture and, as at December 31, 2025, provided in-house technical management for 57 of our Hafnia Vessels and JV Vessels with the remaining 57 Hafnia Vessels and JV Vessels being managed by third-party technical managers.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 20-F Item 5 Operating and Financial Review and Prospects.
competitive_position.claim: Management views its commercial pool strategy as a competitive advantage that improves utilisation and limits idle time relative to non-pooled spot-market peers, achieving a 93.6% utilisation rate and $25,205 TCE income per operating day versus 97.7% and $33,000 in the prior year.
quotes: We believe that our pool employment strategy provides us with a competitive advantage in optimising the earnings of our Hafnia Vessels and TC Vessels.
In addition, our strategy allows us to more efficiently deploy our vessels to limit idle time and provide more stable earnings relative to our non-pooled peers participating in the spot market.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 20-F Item 4.
competitive_position.claim: Through its 50%-owned Seascale Energy Joint Venture with Cargill, Hafnia participates in one of the ten largest bunker procurement companies, which serviced approximately 2,400 vessels after commencing operations.
quotes: By combining the businesses of the Hafnia Bunkers Alliance and Cargill’s Pure Marine Fuels, the Seascale Energy Joint Venture significantly improves such economies of scale and transparency and is now one of the ten largest bunker procurement companies.
Since commencing operations in May 2025, the Seascale Energy Joint Venture serviced approximately 2,400 vessels during the year.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 20-F Item 4 Competitive Landscape.
competitive_position.claim: Hafnia competes in a highly fragmented market against other publicly listed companies, major oil companies, state-controlled entities, and private shipowners on price, vessel location, size, age, condition, and operator reputation.
quotes: We compete against other owners and operators of chemical and product tankers in a market where ownership is highly fragmented and our competitors include other publicly listed companies, major oil companies, state-controlled entities and private shipowners.
We compete for charters on the basis of price, vessel location, size, age and condition of the product tankers as well as our reputation as an operator.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 20-F Item 4 and Item 3.D.
competitive_position.claim: Hafnia acquired 14,156,061 Class A shares of TORM plc, representing approximately 13.97% of TORM's issued share capital, for $311.4 million in aggregate consideration to evaluate strategic opportunities including a potential business combination.
quotes: On September 11, 2025, we entered into a sale and purchase agreement with OCM Njord Holdings S.ar.l. to purchase 14,156,061 Class A Shares of TORM plc (the “TORM Class A Shares”) corresponding to, as of the date of this Annual Report, approximately 13.97% of TORM plc’s issued share capital (the “Investment in TORM”), at a price of $22.0 per share, representing $311.4 million in aggregate consideration.

We believe consolidation is positive for the tanker industry generally and are evaluating potential strategic opportunities involving the Investment in TORM, including a range of potential options for a combination of the two businesses.

There can be no assurance that TORM plc and we will pursue, enter or consummate a potential transaction and there are several risks associated with the negotiation, completion and timing of any potential transaction.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 20-F Item 4 Recent Developments.
competitive_position.claim: Hafnia is reshaping its fleet by contracting eight MR newbuild product tankers for approximately US$405 million while selling vessels and planning to wind down its Handy and LR2 pools and exit the Handy segment.
quotes: On April 3, 2026, we announced that we had signed a contract for the construction of eight MR newbuild product tankers from a South Korean shipyard, with a total purchase price of approximately US$405 million, with deliveries expected between the third quarter of 2028 and the second quarter of 2029.
We intend to wind down our Handy and LR2 pool operations in the upcoming financial year.
We will exit the Handy segment upon the completion of the sale of our Handy vessels, while the majority of its owned LR2 vessels will be employed via time charters.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 20-F Item 3.D and Item 5.
competitive_position.claim: Lack of diversification outside the cyclical tanker industry and heavy spot-market exposure—with 74% of the Hafnia Fleet on short-term contracts not normally extending beyond three months—leave earnings vulnerable to freight rate downturns.
quotes: Due to our lack of diversification, adverse developments in the tanker industry have a significantly greater impact on our financial condition and results of operations than if we maintained more diverse assets or lines of business.
As at December 31, 2025, 74% of the vessels in our Hafnia Fleet were operated in the spot market on short-term contracts that normally do not extend beyond three months.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 20-F Item 3.D and Q2/H1 2026 Form 6-K.
competitive_position.claim: Potential tanker capacity oversupply is a threat, with the product tanker newbuild orderbook equal to approximately 18% of the existing world product tanker fleet in tonnage terms and LR2 vessels able to switch from dirty back to clean trades.
quotes: The product tanker newbuild orderbook equalled approximately 18% of the existing world product tanker fleet in tonnage terms at the end of 2025.
Should these vessels return to ‘clean’ trades, the increase in available product tanker tonnage may affect the supply and demand balance for our product tankers.
While newbuild deliveries remain elevated in 2026, the overall supply outlook is more balanced than headline orderbook figures suggest.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 20-F Item 3.D and Q2/H1 2026 Form 6-K.
competitive_position.claim: Geopolitical conflicts and shipping disruptions in the Red Sea, Arabian Gulf, Bab el-Mandeb Strait, and Strait of Hormuz, together with an IEA-forecast 1.6 mb/d global oil demand contraction, threaten trading routes and demand.
quotes: Disruptions to shipping in the Red Sea, Arabian Gulf, and Strait of Hormuz in connection with the conflict between Israel and Hamas and the conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran or other disruptions to commonly used trading routes could have a negative effect on our operations, business, cash flows, financial condition, and results of operation.
The IEA now forecasts global oil demand contracting by 1.6 mb/d in 2026 to 103.3 mb/d, compared with the 0.4 mb/d decline projected in May.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 20-F Item 3.D.
competitive_position.claim: Tariffs, sanctions, and maritime fees—including suspended U.S. and Chinese port fees on linked vessels and U.S. proposals for universal import fees on cargo carried by non-U.S.-built vessels—threaten vessel supply, charter rates, and compliance exposure.
quotes: In November 2025, both the United States and China suspended the respective port fees for a one-year period.

In February 2026, the United States announced America’s Maritime Action Plan according to which universal fees of between 1 to 25 cents per kilogram of cargo imported into the United States by non- U.S.-built vessels could be imposed.

If port fees, import fees or other fees, including fees specifically affecting vessels with links to certain jurisdictions, are imposed in the United States, China or elsewhere, the supply of vessels may be affected, which could affect the available charter rates and which could have an effect on our results of operations.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 20-F Item 3.D.
competitive_position.claim: Hafnia derives a significant portion of its revenue from its top five customers, creating exposure to revenue loss if any of them default or depart.
quotes: We derive a significant portion of our revenue from our top five customers, and the loss or default of any such customers could result in a significant loss of revenue and adversely affect our business.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 20-F Item 3.D.
competitive_position.claim: Long-term shifts toward renewable energy and electric vehicles, potential 'peak oil' demand decline, and possible reductions in capital allocation by lenders and investors to fossil-fuel transporters threaten long-term demand and financing access.
quotes: A shift in or disruption of the consumer demand from oil towards other energy resources such as wind, solar energy and other renewable energy sources, electricity, natural gas, liquefied natural gas, or hydrogen as well as a shift in governmental commitments and support for energy transition programs will potentially negatively affect the demand for our product tankers.
Further, there is a risk that financial institutions and investors will reduce capital allocation to businesses involved in transporting fossil fuels.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 20-F Item 3.D, Item 18/Notes capital risk disclosure, and Q2/H1 2026 Form 6-K.
competitive_position.claim: Substantial ongoing capital expenditure needs for fleet maintenance and replacement, significant debt service obligations, and financing covenants threaten financial flexibility and vessel ownership if earnings deteriorate.
quotes: We have a significant amount of financial debt and servicing our current or future indebtedness limits funds available for other purposes and if we cannot service our debt, we may lose the vessels in our Hafnia Fleet.

Our credit facilities and lease financing agreements contain covenants that may limit our ability to conduct certain activities, and further, we may be unable to comply with such covenants, which could result in an event of default under the terms of such agreements.
During the financial years ended 31 December 2025, 2024 and 2023, the Group is in compliance with all externally imposed capital requirements.
Our net Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio further decreased from 20.2% in the first quarter to 13.0%, primarily due to strong cash flow generation from both operations and vessel sales.

growth_thesis.claim: Tanker demand growth requires global oil demand to recover after an IEA forecast of a 1.6 mb/d contraction, with an expansion of 2.4 mb/d expected the following year.

growth_thesis.claim: Freight rate growth requires effective clean tanker supply to stay balanced by vessel scrapping, expansion of the sanctioned fleet, and LR2 vessels trading in crude despite an orderbook equal to 18% of the existing fleet.
quotes: While newbuild deliveries remain elevated in 2026, the overall supply outlook is more balanced than headline orderbook figures suggest.
Scrapping potential is increasing as the global fleet ages, and the sanctioned fleet continues to expand, with much of that tonnage unlikely to return to mainstream trading.
A significant share of the product tanker orderbook comprises LR2 vessels, many of which trade in the crude segment, further tightening effective supply within the clean market.
The product tanker newbuild orderbook equalled approximately 18% of the existing world product tanker fleet in tonnage terms at the end of 2025.

growth_thesis.claim: Hafnia operates 74% of its Hafnia Fleet in the spot market and commercial pools to capture rising freight rates and retain fuel savings on voyage charters.
quotes: As at December 31, 2025, 74% of the vessels in our Hafnia Fleet were operated in the spot market on short-term contracts that normally do not extend beyond three months.

We strategically employ our Hafnia Vessels and TC Vessels in pools that are primarily focused on spot market voyage charters, which we believe positions us to capitalise on improving rates in the product tanker market.

Importantly, our pool employment strategy will also allow us to directly benefit from the anticipated fuel savings of our newbuild vessels, as under spot market voyage charters we are responsible for all voyage expenses, including bunker fuel costs, which are generally the largest expense.

growth_thesis.claim: Sustaining earnings from spot-oriented pool deployment requires spot freight rates to stay remunerative and vessel supply and charter rates not to be disrupted by new port or import fees.
quotes: Therefore, any adverse changes in the spot market hire or freight rates may significantly impact our revenue and financial condition.

If port fees, import fees or other fees, including fees specifically affecting vessels with links to certain jurisdictions, are imposed in the United States, China or elsewhere, the supply of vessels may be affected, which could affect the available charter rates and which could have an effect on our results of operations.

Each of the four vessels in the Ecomar Joint Venture are to be time chartered to Total on long-term time charters.

growth_thesis.claim: Delivering growth from newbuild fleet expansion requires timely shipyard construction without non-deliveries and continued access to capital and borrowing to fund capital expenditures.

If we do not set aside funds or are unable to borrow or raise funds in the future or if we are unable to correctly time our capital expenditures, it may adversely affect our revenue, business, results of operations, financial condition and available cash.

quotes: In April 2025, the U.S. Trade Representative (“USTR”) introduced port fees to be charged in respect of U.S. port calls by vessels with links to China, including Chinese-built vessels and vessels owned or operated by Chinese entities.
In November 2025, both the United States and China suspended the respective port fees for a one-year period.

In February 2026, the United States announced America’s Maritime Action Plan according to which universal fees of between 1 to 25 cents per kilogram of cargo imported into the United States by non- U.S.-built vessels could be imposed.

We are subject to complex laws and regulations, including environmental laws and regulations, that can increase our liability and adversely affect our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition, and our available cash.
